newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel receives Turkish jets in upgrade deal.
newsitem.headline: Israel receives Turkish jets in upgrade deal.

text.p: Israel Aircraft Industries has received the first of 54 Turkish F-4 Phantom jets under a $600 million deal to upgrade the Turkish Air Force's fleet, the company said on Wednesday.
The announcement coincided with the visit of Turkish armed forces chief General Ismail Hakki Karadayi to IAI as part of a three-day visit to the Jewish state.

"We are very proud of this important visit which has symbolic importance: It comes only two days after the arrival of the first two Phantoms from Turkey," IAI chief Moshe Keret was quoted as saying in a company statement.
"This is the first practical stage of upgrading the Turkish Airforce's Phantom jets," the statement said.

IAI agreed with Turkey in 1995 to upgrade 54 McDonnell Douglas F-4 jets. The deal was a boost for Israel's defence industry and a sign of strengthening ties between mainly Moslem but secular Turkey and the Jewish state.
The five-year deal to upgrade the fighter bombers will involve installation of advanced avionic systems, including radar and electronic warfare and navigation systems.
In addition to the Phantom deal, Israel and Turkey have signed an accord that lets Israeli jets train in Turkish airspace.
The accords were condemned by Iran and many in the Arab world. Ankara's closer links with Israel also drew strong protests from Islamists in Turkey.
But since becoming prime minister eight months ago Turkey's Islamist Welfare Party leader Necmettin Erbakan has toned down his criticism.
Karadayi told Israel's Haaretz newspaper before his visit began on Monday that Turkey's secular structure was rooted in the country's constitution and would not change.
